# Inter-rater agreement: Krippendorff's alpha, kappa and ICC

> Free online inter-rater reliability tool. Paste ratings from two or more raters, coders or annotators (a column per rater, subject-rater-rating rows, or a counts table) and it reports Krippendorff's alpha (nominal, ordinal, interval or ratio, missing ratings allowed) with a bootstrap interval, Cohen's kappa with linear and quadratic weights and its standard error, Fleiss' kappa and Gwet's AC1/AC2, pairwise and per-category kappa, alpha with each rater left out, the subjects raters split on, and the six intraclass correlations (Shrout & Fleiss 1979) with McGraw & Wong's intervals. Matches the krippendorff, irrCAC, statsmodels, scikit-learn and pingouin packages, and reproduces Krippendorff's (2011) and Shrout & Fleiss's published examples. Runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are statistical estimates from the data you supply, not legal, tax, financial, medical or professional advice. Agreement between raters is not proof that they are right.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/inter-rater-agreement/)

## Use it from code

- `node cli.mjs ratings.csv [--layout auto|wide|long|counts] [--scale auto|nominal|ordinal|interval|ratio] [--categories a,b,c] [--bootstrap 1000] [--seed 1] [--confidence 0.95] [--csv|--json]`
- `node platform/agents/tools.mjs call inter-rater-agreement analyze --input '{"ratings":[[1,1,2],[2,2,2],[3,2,3],[1,1,1]]}'` (or `{"csv":"..."}`, `{"long":[{"item":"a","rater":"x","rating":"yes"}]}`, `{"counts":[[3,0],[1,2]],"categories":["yes","no"]}`)
- From JavaScript: `krippendorffAlpha(counts, values, metric)`, `fleissKappa(counts, W)`, `gwetAC(counts, W)`, `cohenKappa(a, b, q, W)`, `icc(matrix)`.

## What it answers

- Do my coders agree beyond chance, and is that enough to publish (Krippendorff's 0.667 and 0.800)?
- What is Cohen's kappa, weighted kappa, Fleiss' kappa or the ICC for these ratings, with an interval?
- Why is kappa low when raw agreement is high (the kappa paradox), and what does Gwet's AC1 say?
- Which category do raters confuse, and which rater disagrees with the rest?
- Which ICC form fits my design (one-way, two-way random, two-way mixed; single or average)?
